name: nextjs
summary: Next.js structure that preserves an existing root/src and App/Pages Router layout while organizing features, components, server/data services, models, and tests.
dependency_direction: app routes -> features -> components/services/models/lib. Server-only code must not leak into client components.

folders.responsibility: Next.js routes, layouts, loading/error boundaries, route handlers when appropriate.
folders.allowed: Route segments, layouts, metadata, server/client boundary composition.
folders.avoid: Large business logic directly inside route files.

folders.allowed: Feature UI, feature actions, feature state, feature-specific composition.

folders.avoid: Server data fetching unless explicitly designed.

folders.responsibility: Data access, API clients, server actions, external service adapters.
folders.allowed: Server-only adapters, fetch clients, auth/data wrappers.

folders.responsibility: Shared types, validation schemas, and DTOs.
folders.allowed: Zod schemas, TypeScript types, domain models.
Pure utilities, config helpers, formatting helpers.
folders.avoid: A dumping ground for feature logic.

folders.allowed: Vitest/Jest/Playwright tests as project conventions allow.

rules: Preserve the project's existing root or src placement and App/Pages Router choice; do not create a competing router root.
Preserve the existing framework, design system, and component conventions. For greenfield choices, use semantic HTML and accessible, maintainable styling that fits the product.
Keep route files thin when feature logic grows.
Use official Next/React guidance for data fetching and rendering changes.
If the project already uses a CSS framework, follow the existing convention; if it does not, add one only for a demonstrated need and with authorization.
When visual direction is incomplete, preserve existing tokens or propose a coherent option and label assumptions; do not force a separate structural-baseline phase.
validation: Inspect package scripts before running lint/test/build.
Use browser verification for visible UI changes.
